about: Disc images worth burning, picked for people who remember when a CD-R was cutting-edge technology. Every image here may be freely redistributed. The depot only links to each project's own downloads; a monthly job fetches every image, records its size and SHA-256, and Krouton refuses a download that doesn't match.

channels.title: The shelf, 1998 to 2010
channels.about: Systems from the years when a burner was the fastest way to share software and every magazine came with a disc.

channels.title: Strange and wonderful
channels.about: Tiny systems, whole operating systems written in assembly, and a Linux that saves itself back onto the disc it booted from.

channels.title: Fix-it discs
channels.about: Boot a broken computer, test its memory, rescue its files, or wipe it before it leaves the house.

channels.title: Console homebrew
channels.about: Open-source tools for the GameCube, Wii, Dreamcast and PlayStation: boot discs that burn on a CD-R or DVD-R, and SD-card tools for making 1:1 backups of discs you own. No games: bring your own. A Wii only reads burned DVDs with a modchip, and only on the early drive models; DVD+R discs also need their book type set to DVD-ROM, which Krouton can do.

items.title: The Homebrew Channel (HackMii Installer)
items.summary: Where Wii homebrew starts: it installs the Homebrew Channel and BootMii, from which CleanRip and USB Loader GX run. The installer is free but its authors only offer it from their own site.
items.license: Free to use; redistribution not permitted

items.title: Wiimms ISO Tools (wit)
items.summary: Command-line tools for checking, converting and extracting Wii and GameCube images: ISO, WBFS, CISO and more. Useful for checking a dump before burning or copying it.
